![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14253263/assets/984b29e4fa91543e74b6dec14794d2c46175633ab1118a67246e015055177182.png)

Find the total area bounded by the polar curve $r=\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta ),$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to find the interval for $\theta $ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta ) & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta ) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two solutions for $5\theta \in [0,2\pi ]$:

$$
5\theta =0,\pi \,⟹\,\theta =0,\frac{\pi }{5}
$$

As a result, the first petal is traversed for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{5}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14253263/assets/e41fe5bc79759e102339e1824d82691c45fb454a86b1ca4674b1d6ba5770c107.png)

Since there are $5$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =5\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =5\cdot 3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}{sin}^{2}⁡(5\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =15\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(10\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{15}{2}{(\theta -\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(10\theta ))|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =\frac{15}{2}[(\frac{\pi }{5}-\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi ))-(0-\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))] \\  & =\frac{15}{2}(\frac{\pi }{5}-0) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$
